source.title: საქართველოს მთავრობის დადგენილება №424 — მიწისქვეშა მტკნარი სასმელი წყლის მოპოვების მიზნით ჭაბურღილების აღრიცხვის წესი

scope.purpose: მიწისქვეშა მტკნარი სასმელი წყლის მოპოვების მიზნით ჭაბურღილების სახელმწიფო აღრიცხვა
scope.household_exemption_review_scope: Article 2 of Decree 424 only; this is not a conclusion about other legislation.

claims.label: FACT
claims.claim: The regulation applies to wells deeper than 20 metres drilled for extraction of fresh drinking groundwater, subject to the stated effective-date scope.

claims.label: FACT
claims.claim: The scope includes wells that produce expected quantity and quality, wells that fail to produce expected quantity and/or quality, and wells that produce no groundwater.

claims.label: FACT
claims.claim: Mineral, thermal and therapeutic-balneological groundwater and fresh-drinking-water wells drilled before 2026-09-01 are excluded by Article 2(2).

claims.label: FACT
claims.claim: The driller submits the annex information within 15 working days after drilling completion; NEA notifies the driller within 10 working days after receipt that information has been placed in the hydrogeological database.

claims.label: FACT
claims.claim: The annex contains exact UTM WGS 1984 well coordinates, cadastral code where available, owner and driller identifiers, contact details, addresses and technical/hydrogeological fields.

claims.label: FACT
claims.claim: The annex explicitly allows the field-sampling and laboratory-analysis states to be recorded as not sampled; NEA may conduct monitoring and sampling as needed.

claims.label: FACT
claims.claim: The owner signs to confirm personal-data accuracy and consent to share personal and well technical information with NEA.
claims.reference: Article 6(1)(b) and owner signature/consent in Annex

claims.label: INFERENCE
claims.claim: A registry entry alone is not evidence that the water has passed a drinking-water potability assessment because sampling and laboratory-result fields may be marked not sampled.

claims.label: INFERENCE
claims.claim: The consent clause names NEA; it does not establish a separate legal basis or consent for NOEMA to obtain or process identifiable registry records.
claims.reference: Article 6(1)(b); third-party processing basis remains to be assessed

claims.label: UNTESTED IDEA
claims.claim: AquaSignal should maintain a private identity vault, pseudonymous well IDs, explicit sample-state transitions and aggregate-only public releases after authorization and privacy review.
claims.reference: NOEMA architecture proposal; not a requirement stated by Decree 424

limitations: Only the official Matsne text and annex were reviewed; no live state-register data or API was accessed.
The decree does not establish that the register is publicly downloadable; access and reuse permissions remain unverified.
No real well records, coordinates, cadastral codes, owner or driller identifiers, contact details or sample results are included.
The legal consent clause names NEA; third-party processing rights and any other legal basis require separate legal review.
No operational audit established whether NEA's register is populated, complete, accurate or routinely updated.
This is a research and data-governance note, not legal advice or a drinking-water quality assessment.
